title: 送元二使安西
titleEn: Seeing Yuan the Second Off on a Mission to Anxi
author: 王维
intro: A morning farewell at an inn outside Chang’an: fresh rain, green willows, one last cup of wine — because beyond Yang Pass there will be no old friends. For centuries this was the farewell song in China.
analysis: 王维的朋友元二要出使安西（今天新疆一带），王维在渭城（长安西北）为他送行。前两句写送别的早晨：一场小雨刚好打湿了路上的尘土，旅店旁边的柳树被雨洗过，绿得发亮。景色清新明朗，并不悲伤；可是“柳”谐音“留”，古人送别常折柳相赠，所以青青柳色里已经藏着“不想让你走”的心意。后两句是送别酒桌上的一句话：“再喝完这一杯吧，向西出了阳关，就再也没有老朋友了。”前面一定已经喝了很多杯，这“更尽一杯”写出了舍不得分开、一拖再拖的心情。阳关之外是荒凉的沙漠，路远又危险，这句劝酒的话又亲切又沉重。这首诗后来被谱成歌曲《阳关三叠》，成为古人送别时最常唱的歌。
analysisEn: Wang Wei’s friend Yuan, “the Second” (the second son of his family), is leaving on an official mission to Anxi, the Tang military command in the far west, in today’s Xinjiang. They say goodbye at Weicheng, the first stop northwest of Chang’an. The first two lines set a fresh morning scene: a light rain has just settled the dust on the road, and the willows by the inn, washed clean, are a brilliant green. Nothing here sounds sad. But willow (柳 liǔ) sounds like “stay” (留 liú), and friends traditionally gave each other a willow twig at parting, so the green willows quietly say “I wish you didn’t have to go.” The second half is simply one sentence spoken at the table: “Have one more cup — once you go west through Yang Pass, there will be no old friends.” “One more” tells us they have already been drinking for a while and neither wants to stand up. Yang Pass was the gateway to the desert; beyond it lay a long, dangerous road among strangers. That is why this plain, warm toast hits so hard. The poem was set to music as “Three Refrains at Yang Pass” (阳关三叠) and became the standard song of farewell; it is also known as “Song of Weicheng”.
background: Wang Wei (701?–761) served as an official in the Tang capital. Nothing is known of Yuan the Second beyond this poem; Anxi was the Tang Protectorate governing the Western Regions, a journey of months from Chang’an.
pronunciation: “朝雨”的“朝”读 zhāo（早晨）。“浥”读 yì（湿润）。“客舍”的“舍”读 shè。“更尽”的“更”读 gèng（再）。题目“使安西”的“使”读 shǐ（出使）。
version: 采用统编小学语文教材版本。题目一作《渭城曲》，谱曲后称《阳关三叠》。

lines.py: wèi chéng zhāo yǔ yì qīng chén
lines.lit: In Weicheng, the morning rain moistens the light dust;
lines.en: Morning rain in Weicheng has settled the light dust;

lines.py: kè shè qīng qīng liǔ sè xīn
lines.lit: by the inn, green, green, the willows’ colour is fresh.
lines.en: by the inn the willows are green, washed new.

lines.py: quàn jūn gèng jìn yī bēi jiǔ
lines.lit: I urge you to finish one more cup of wine:
lines.en: Come, drink one more cup with me —

lines.py: xī chū yáng guān wú gù rén
lines.lit: going west out of Yang Pass, there will be no old friends.
lines.en: west of Yang Pass, you will find no old friends.

words.en: to go on an official mission
words.note: 古义“出使”；现代汉语“大使”“使者”。

words.en: Anxi, the Tang command in the far west
words.note: 唐代安西都护府，在今新疆。
今陕西咸阳东北，在渭水北岸。
古代旅店；现代汉语说“旅馆”“客栈”。
青：古代可指绿色、蓝色或黑色，这里是绿。
读 gèng，这里是“再”的意思。

words.en: to finish (a cup); to drink up
Yang Pass, gateway to the western desert

words.note: 古义；现代汉语“故人”多指已故的人。

imagery.name: 雨
imagery.zh: 一场早晨的小雨洗净了尘土，让送别的画面清新明亮，不落俗套。
imagery.en: A light morning rain washes the dust away, making the farewell scene fresh and clear rather than gloomy.

imagery.name: 柳
imagery.zh: 客舍旁的青青柳色，暗含折柳送别、“柳”谐“留”的意思：舍不得朋友走。
imagery.en: The green willows by the inn carry the custom of giving a willow twig at parting — 柳 sounds like 留, “stay”.

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: “更尽一杯酒”：一杯接一杯，是想把分别的时刻再拖长一点。
imagery.en: “One more cup”: each extra cup is a way to put off the moment of parting a little longer.

imagery.name: 关
imagery.zh: 阳关是熟悉世界的尽头，出了关就是荒凉陌生的远方。
imagery.en: Yang Pass marks the end of the familiar world; beyond it lie desert and strangers.
